newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan prosecutors indict Hamanaka in forgery case.
newsitem.headline: Japan prosecutors indict Hamanaka in forgery case.

text.p: Japanese prosecutors said on Tuesday that they had indicted Sumitomo Corp's former star copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka on four charges of forgery.

The move follows Sumitomo's announcement earlier on Tuesday that it had filed a complaint against Hamanaka with prosecutors alleging fraud, which potentially carries a more serious penalty than forgery.
Hamanaka was arrested on October 22 on suspicion that he forged two documents in 1994 in connection with Sumitomo's estimated $2.6 billion loss from copper trades.

Tuesday's indictment included two additional charges that Hamanaka forged a Sumitomo managing director's signature on documents in the fall of 1993, said Tatsuo Kainaka, deputy chief prosecutor of the Tokyo District Prosecutor's Office.

According to a statement issued by the prosecutors' office, the two additional counts involved a document dated September 30, 1993, verifying the sale of copper call options to Credit Lyonnais Rouse through Winchester Brokerage Ltd, and a document dated November 17, 1993, offering warrants held by Sumitomo as collateral for obligations to Credit Lyonnais Rouse.

The other two counts, detailed in the prosecutors' office's October 22 statement on Hamanaka's arrest, involved two letters in 1994 stating Hamanaka had the authority to enter into certain metals transactions and to designate recipients of funds deposited with firms in the Merrill Lynch group.
